language_wrapper: Let base {base} be an integer greater than 2. Define f(x) on positive integers by f(1)=1, f(x)=x/{base} if {base} divides x, and f(x)=x+1 otherwise. For a given x, define the sequence x_1=x and x_{n+1}=f(x_n), and let d(x) be the smallest n such that x_n=1. Let m be the number of positive integers x such that d(x)={target_steps}. Compute the sum of the distinct prime factors of m.
hardness_rationale: The seed problem works in base 10 with a single divide-by-10 rule and asks for a specific target depth. This family generalizes the process to an arbitrary base b, requiring analysis of carry propagation across base-b digits. A correct solution needs to model the evolution of the last digit, its carry into higher digits, and count digit configurations whose aggregate transition cost equals the specified target steps. The counting reduces to constrained compositions with mixed bounds (final digit bound differs from interior digits), handled via dynamic programming. Compared to the seed, this demands a deeper understanding of the digit-carry automaton in general base, a nontrivial summation over lengths and first-nonzero positions, and a careful combinatorial count—not solvable by simple pattern spotting or guessing.
notes: Counting approach: If x has base-b digits d_k...d_0 and J is the index of the first nonzero digit, then the total number of transitions T=d(x)-1 equals (k+1) plus (b - d_J) plus, for j>J, b - ((d_j + 1) mod b) when that is nonzero. This is equivalent to summing a first part in [1..b-1] and tail parts in [0..b-1] except the highest tail digit cannot take b-1. From this, we count all pairs (k,J) and tail sequences achieving the target sum via DP. The verifier enforces that instances are nontrivial by rejecting cases with too-small m or only one prime factor.
source_question: For all positive integers $x$ , let \[f(x)=\begin{cases}1 &\mbox{if }x = 1\\ \frac x{10} &\mbox{if }x\mbox{ is divisible by 10}\\ x+1 &\mbox{otherwise}\end{cases}\] and define a sequence as follows: $x_1=x$ and $x_{n+1}=f(x_n)$ for all positive integers $n$ . Let $d(x)$ be the smallest $n$ such that $x_n=1$ . (For example, $d(100)=3$ and $d(87)=7$ .) Let $m$ be the number of positive integers $x$ such that $d(x)=20$ . Find the sum of the distinct prime factors of $m$ .
